short: A brief Jacobite rebellion supported by Spain that was crushed at the Battle of Glen Shiel.
full:
In 1719, the Spanish government, at war with Britain over territorial disputes, agreed to support a Jacobite invasion. The plan envisioned a main force landing in England, accompanied by a diversionary landing in the Scottish Highlands. A small force of Spanish marines and Jacobite exiles successfully landed in Scotland in March, but the main fleet was destroyed by storms and never arrived.

The isolated Highland contingent managed to raise a few local clans but was swiftly confronted by government troops. On 10 June 1719, the Jacobite and Spanish forces were decisively defeated at the Battle of Glen Shiel. The Spanish marines surrendered, the Highlanders dispersed, and the brief "Nineteen" uprising was extinguished.
